question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to $\sin(x - 4)\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}-\left(12 x - 48\right)\sin(x - 4)=\cos(x - 4)$ that satisfies $y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 4)=3 \pi^{2}$. Assume that $4<x<\pi + 4$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first rearrange and separate, then integrate and apply the initial condition.

$$
y'=\frac{\cos(x - 4)}{\sin(x - 4)}+12 x - 48.
$$

Use $v=\sin(x - 4)$, so $\mathrm{d}v=\cos(x - 4)\mathrm{d}x$. On the given interval, sine is positive. Thus

$$
\int\mathrm{d}y=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{v}+\int \left(12 x - 48\right)\mathrm{d}x.
$$

$$
y=\ln(\sin(x - 4))+6 \left(x - 4\right)^{2}+C.
$$

At $x=\frac{\pi}{2} + 4$, $\sin(x - 4)=1$ and hence

$$
3 \pi^{2}=\frac{3 \pi^{2}}{2}+C,\qquad C=\frac{3 \pi^{2}}{2}.
$$

Therefore $y=6 \left(x - 4\right)^{2} + \ln{\left(\sin{\left(x - 4 \right)} \right)} + \frac{3 \pi^{2}}{2}$.
